ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, ABCD is drawn as a square or an axis-aligned quadrilateral, the right-side AB is on the vertical straight line g, and the left-side CD is also a vertical line segment and is parallel to g; C is at the upper left, D is at the lower left, E is located to the left of CD, and line segments EC and ED form triangle ECD. Then reason: The problem gives that the side length of ABCD is 4 cm, so the area of square ABCD is 4×4=16 cm². Also because the area of triangle ECD is the same as ABCD, the area of triangle ECD is also 16 cm². Taking CD as the base of triangle ECD, CD=4 cm, and its height is the horizontal perpendicular distance h from point E to line CD. From the area formula (1/2)×4×h=16, we get h=8 cm. The horizontal distance from line CD to line g equals the side length of the square, 4 cm. Therefore the perpendicular distance from point E to line g is 8+4=12 cm.

raw_record.question_text: The quadrilateral $ABCD$ with side length $4\mathrm{~cm}$ has the same area as triangle $ECD$. What is the perpendicular distance from point $E$ to the line $g$?

method.method_draft: Read from the image that ABCD is a square/axis-aligned quadrilateral with AB on the vertical line g, CD parallel to g on the left, and E lies to the left of CD; triangle ECD uses CD as its vertical base. Read from the text that every side of ABCD is 4 cm and that area(ABCD) = area(ECD). Since ABCD is a square of side 4, its area is 16 cm^2. In triangle ECD, take CD = 4 cm as the base; its perpendicular height is the horizontal distance from E to line CD. Solve (1/2)(4)(height) = 16 to get height = 8 cm. The desired perpendicular distance from E to line g is this 8 cm plus the horizontal distance from CD to g, which is the side length 4 cm. Therefore the distance is 12 cm.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate setup based on the image. Read that line g is vertical through side AB, and ABCD is a 4 cm square extending left from g, with A and B on g and C,D on the vertical line 4 cm left of g. Assign coordinates, for example A=(0,0), B=(0,4), C=(-4,4), D=(-4,0), so line g is x=0. Let E=(x,y), with x<-4 as shown. Read from the text that area(ECD) equals the square area 4^2=16. Since C and D have the same x-coordinate and CD has length 4, the area of triangle ECD is 1/2·4·|x+4|. Set 2|x+4|=16, giving |x+4|=8. Because E is left of CD, x=-12. The perpendicular distance from E to g, i.e. to x=0, is |x|=12 cm.
